one_liner: Generated-CUDA PyTorch backend for equivariant tensor-product graph convolutions; claims 1.2x-49.7x over OpenEquivariance with bounded memory.
what_it_does: Sobek computes the edge-conditioned equivariant tensor-product convolution used in e3nn-style interatomic potentials (NequIP/MACE-like layers): radial projection, spherical-harmonic coupling and sum over neighbours, with forward, backward and double backward under PyTorch autograd. It is not a drop-in for e3nn or OpenEquivariance: the TPConv module takes the compact per-edge radial embedding phi plus the final radial projection matrix (owned internally or passed as radial_linear) instead of a precomputed [num_edges, weight_numel] weight tensor, and its native feature layout is ir_mul (to_ir_mul / to_mul_ir adapters provided). Extras are TPConvGraph (reusable receiver/source CSR) and TPConvCUDAGraph (fixed-shape CUDA Graph capture up to double backward).
how_it_is_fast: It fuses the last radial linear layer into the convolution and reassociates the computation so edge-local products are reduced straight into bounded receiver-side state, so the per-edge weight tensor, per-edge messages and their adjoints are never materialized. Per-problem CUDA kernels are code-generated from the irreps/instruction spec and JIT-compiled with nvcc -O3 via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline, combined with cuBLAS GEMMs; graph traversal is receiver-owned (CSR by receiver, with a source-ordered pass for gradients), deterministic and atomic-free. A receiver_scratch_bytes budget (default 128 MiB) drives node-chunking and a knapsack-style choice of which receiver aggregates to retain for the backward pass.
when_to_use: Training equivariant GNN potentials in PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs where force training needs double backward and memory, not FLOPs, limits graph size.
Large or dense graphs (many edges per node, wide irreps) where materializing [E, weight_numel] edge weights blows past GPU memory with OpenEquivariance or e3nn.
Models whose last radial MLP layer can be handed to the convolution (phi plus projection weight), so the fusion boundary fits.
Fixed-topology workloads (MD steps on one structure) that benefit from TPConvGraph reuse and CUDA Graph replay.
Runs that need bitwise-deterministic results, since the kernels avoid atomics.
when_not_to_use: Anything other than float32: no fp64, fp16 or bf16 path (GEMMs can only switch between ieee and tf32).

Problems that mix uvw and uvu paths in one instruction set, or uvu with unequal input/output multiplicities or spherical-harmonic multiplicity above one; only weighted fully connected uvw and homogeneous channel-wise uvu are supported.
Non-NVIDIA hardware or environments without a CUDA toolkit for JIT compilation; every new problem shape pays a first-call nvcc compile.
Production use that needs maturity: version 0.1.0, 5 commits (2026-07-20 to 2026-07-24), no releases, no issue history, single-company authorship.
Pipelines already built around e3nn/OpenEquivariance's precomputed edge-weight interface and mul_ir layout; using mul_ir mode in Sobek adds transposes and emits an efficiency warning.

integration.dependencies: Python >= 3.11, PyTorch >= 2.12 with CUDA, cgen >= 2025.1, a CUDA toolkit usable by PyTorch's JIT extension builder (13.3 recommended); benchmarks extra adds e3nn, OpenEquivariance, torch-geometric 2.8.0, numpy, matplotlib
integration.min_toolchain: Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.12, CUDA Toolkit (13.3 recommended; 12.9 builds about 25% slower per README)
integration.platforms: NVIDIA CUDA GPUs only (kernels compiled for the local arch via PyTorch's arch flags)
integration.thread_safety: not documented (generated CUDA dumps are written atomically; CUDA Graph replay returns session-owned storage overwritten by the next replay unless clone=True)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same mathematical operator and e3nn-style irreps/instruction tuples, but a different call signature (phi plus radial_linear instead of per-edge weights) and a different native feature layout (ir_mul)

gotchas: First call for each new tensor-product specification compiles CUDA; the extension is cached only when PyTorch, CUDA, GPU arch, problem and codegen settings all match.
The CUDA toolkit is chosen from CUDA_HOME; the README reports identical kernels about 25% slower when built with CUDA 12.9 instead of 13.3.
TPConvGraph tensors must not be modified in place, and a user-supplied sender_perm is only structurally checked, not validated as a permutation.
phi_dim not divisible by four disables aligned float4 radial-embedding loads in receiver-side kernels.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Sobek over OpenEquivariance, cuEquivariance or FlashTP when the per-edge weight tensor is what runs you out of memory or you need double backward at scale and can fuse the final radial layer; pick cuEquivariance or OpenEquivariance for drop-in e3nn compatibility, other dtypes, or a mature dependency, and FlashTP for its published SevenNet end-to-end results (Sobek reports no FlashTP comparison).
verified_claims_summary: The authors' preprint (arXiv 2607.18074, read only through search snippets) reports Sobek faster in all 75 OpenEquivariance-capacity-matched comparisons (UVW 16-profile and UVU 9-profile grids, forward, backward and double backward), 1.2x to 49.7x, with up to 99% lower peak allocated memory, on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 in fp32 per a search snippet. The repo's harness (sobek/benchmarks/measure.py, runners.py) times medians of CUDA-event samples after warmup, and by default times OpenEquivariance including the phi @ radial_linear weight expansion and receiver sort (an oe_preexpanded variant excludes the expansion); no result files are checked in and the nvcc flags are -O3 plus PyTorch arch flags.
status_note: Apache-2.0, version 0.1.0 published in July 2026 by Cortex Discovery GmbH with 12 stars and no activity since 2026-07-24; usable as a pip-installable PyTorch module but young enough to pin and validate against e3nn before trusting it.
